title: Polynomial-Time Gate-State Update
statement: The bit-string update that leaves a state unchanged when its work word is done, otherwise checks whether that word is valid, and then either advances the computation by updating the encoded work word, counter, and value list or resets the work word as specified, is polynomial-time computable. That is, a deterministic Turing machine with finitely many states computes this update on every bit-string input in at most $C(n+1)^c$ steps for some $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, where $n$ is the input length.
